clues.text: This town sits on the south bank of a big river. Two small rivers join just upstream to form it.
clues.narrowing: Points to a river city just below the meeting of two rivers.

source.quote: Downtown Montgomery lies along the southern bank of the Alabama River, about 6 miles (10 km) downstream from the confluence of the Coosa and Tallapoosa rivers.

clues.text: Winters here are short and mild, but summers stretch on long, hot, and humid. On most summer days the heat climbs past 90 degrees.
clues.narrowing: Rules out northern capitals; keeps hot, humid southern river cities.

source.quote: Montgomery has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen Cfa), with short, mild winters, warm springs and autumns, and long, hot, humid summers.

clues.text: In 1846, the state moved its capital here from an old town. Cotton farms had grown rich, and power had moved south.
clues.narrowing: Cuts the list to the city that took the capital from Tuscaloosa in 1846.

source.quote: The state capital was moved from Tuscaloosa to Montgomery, on January 28, 1846.

clues.text: In 1955, Rosa Parks would not give up her bus seat to a white man. She was put in jail, and a bus boycott that changed the land began.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: the Rosa Parks bus boycott began in one southern capital.

source.quote: On December 1, 1955, Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her bus seat to a white man, sparking the Montgomery bus boycott.

clues.text: The governor of Alabama works in this town. Its lawmakers meet here in the capitol, on a hill.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and lawmakers of Alabama work in this city.

source.quote: is the capital city of the U.S. state of Alabama

reveal.blurb: This river city became the state capital in 1846, and for a short time in 1861 it was even the first capital of the Confederacy. A century later, Rosa Parks' bus arrest here sparked a boycott that changed the country. The building is the capitol, and the city is the capital. Montgomery is the capital of Alabama.
